entities.description: Fatal crowd crush on 2003-02-17 at the E2 nightclub, 2347 S. Michigan Ave., Chicago; 21 dead, 50+ injured.
Black-owned second-floor nightclub (8,000 sq ft) above the Epitome restaurant; operated May 2000 – Feb 2003.
Upscale restaurant on the first floor of 2347 S. Michigan; same owners as E2; closed permanently after the tragedy.
1910 Fiat showroom; contributing property of the Motor Row Historic District; housed Le Mirage, Hero's, the Clique, Epitome/E2; vacant 2003–2024; demolished Dec 2024.
entities.note: Building is a separate entity from the venue (audit near-miss rule).

entities.description: Co-owner of E2/Epitome; attorney; name on business paperwork. Manslaughter charges dropped 2008; contempt convicted 2009 (reinstated 2013); resentenced 2015 to probation.
Co-owner ('operations guy') of E2/Epitome; silent partner (convicted felon, could not hold tavern license). Manslaughter acquitted 2007; contempt convicted 2009 (reinstated 2013); resentenced 2015.
E2 club manager; son of Calvin Hollins Jr. Acquitted of involuntary manslaughter Jan 2007 (directed verdict).
Party promoter (Envy Entertainment) the night of the tragedy. Acquitted of involuntary manslaughter Jan 2007 (directed verdict).
Promoter of the party at E2 on 2003-02-17; hired ten security guards.

entities.canonical_name: The 21 victims of the E2 stampede
entities.description: Twelve women and nine men, ages 21–43 (19–43 per one source), who died of compressional asphyxia on 2003-02-17. Memorialized collectively per CTL dignity policy; 30 children lost a parent.
entities.note: Individual victims named in the dossier only where families spoke in reputable reporting (Nicole Rainey; DaShand Howard; Demetricta Carwell).

entities.description: E2 security guard who testified he deployed pepper spray to break up a fight of ~15 patrons; said he was trained by the Illinois Police Reserve Patrol.
entities.note: Identity single-threaded via Tribune/Wikipedia citation chain.

entities.description: Issued the July 2002 closure order; prosecuted the contempt case; enacted the 2003 indoor pepper-spray ordinance; sued by victims' families (dismissed by 2013) and countersued by the owners.
21-count charges against Kyles, Hollins Jr., Hollins III, Flores. Three acquitted by directed verdict (Judge Dennis Porter, Jan 2007); Kyles's charges dropped 2008. Status: closed.

Indirect criminal contempt for violating the July 2002 closure order. Convicted Nov 25, 2009 (2 yrs); vacated Nov 16, 2011; reinstated by IL Supreme Court Apr 4, 2013 ('certain, clear and concise'); resentenced Nov 20, 2015 (probation + 500 hrs service). Status: closed.
Wrongful-death and injury suits; tentative $1.5M settlement (21 death + 95 injury claims, 2006); $2.5M insurance fund; Clear Channel and city claims; final outcomes unresolved.

entities.canonical_name: Families & Friends of the E2 Victims
entities.description: Family advocacy group founded April 2010 by Howard Ray; presses for accountability and memorialization.
Brother of victim DaShand Howard; Vietnam veteran; founded Families & Friends of the E2 Victims; public advocate questioning the emergency response.
Parent of WGCI-FM; named civil defendant over the allegation that its DJ directed the pepper-spray use; objected to the partial settlement; summary judgment denied 2010.
Mayor Daley–appointed panel (co-chair Atty. Andrea Zopp) reviewing building codes and enforcement after E2; drove 2003–04 reforms.
State law sponsored by then-State Sen. Barack Obama: barred indoor sprays, prohibited blocked exits in clubs, required panic bars at large venues. Statute number not located.
City ordinance adopted spring 2003 banning indoor use of pepper spray or similar substances. Municipal code citation not located.
Purchased 2347 S. Michigan in 2021; plans 21-story senior housing; promised a victims' memorial in the redevelopment.
Fatal nightclub fire, West Warwick, Rhode Island, 2003-02-20; 100 dead. Historically paired with E2; together spurred a national nightclub-safety push. Candidate for future CTL-RD-EVENT dossier.
